?" is the question involved in this case.

Respondent Nos.1 to 3 were prosecuted in Special Case No.57/2014 on the file of I Additional District and Sessions and Special Judge, Mandya for the charges for the offences punishable under Sections 450, 370, 376, 114, 506 r/w Section 34 of IPC and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short 'POCSO Act') on the basis of the charge sheet filed by KR Pete Rural police in Cr.No.77/2014 of their police station.

sentences.text: 3. Respondent Nos.2 and 3 are the father and mother of respondent No.1.
They were accused Nos.1 to 3 in Special Case No.57/2014.
For the purpose of convenience, parties will be referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the trial Court.
4. PW.1 is the alleged victim of the case.
PW.2 is the father and PW7 is the mother of PW.1.
PW3 is the maternal uncle and PW.4 is the paternal uncle of PW1.
The accused, PWs.1, 2 and 7 belong to the same village.
5. The case of the prosecution in brief is as follows:
(i) That accused was the neighbour of the victim.
As on 17.03.2014, PW1 was aged 17 years.

On 17.03.2014 at 8.00 p.m., when PW1 was alone in the house, taking advantage of that, accused No.1 dragged her from her house to a near by abandoned house, criminally intimidating her, committed penetrative sexual assault on her.
PW1 raised alarm, PWs.3 and 4 who were nearby on hearing the commotion rushed to the scene of the offence and witnessed the incident.
On seeing them accused No.1 escaped.
PWs.3 and 4 took the victim to her house and informed PW2 the father of PW1.

When PW2 approached accused Nos.2 and 3 questioning the act of accused No.1, they quarreled with PW2 and said that accused No.1 is a man, he can do State Of Karnataka vs Mahesha on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76233608/
2 anything and conquer the same and they have motivated him to do whatever he wants.
(ii) PW2 filed complaint as per Ex.P5 before PW14 the PSI of KR Pete Rural Police station on 20.03.2014.
On the basis of Ex.P5, PW14 registered the FIR Ex.P6 in Cr.No.77/2014 against accused Nos.1 to 3 for the aforesaid offences.
Then he handed over the further investigation to PW.13, the Circle Police Inspector of KR Pete Rural Police Station.
PW13 conducted the spot mahazar at the place shown by PW1 in the presence of PW8 and CW7.
He got the victim medically examined, on completing the investigation filed the charge sheet.
6. The trial Court on taking cognizance secured the accused.
On hearing both side, the trial Court framed the charges against accused No.1 for the offences punishable under Sections 450, 376 of IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
So far as accused Nos.2 & 3, the trial Court framed the charges against them for the offences punishable under Sections 370, 114, 506 r/w Section 34 of IPC.
The accused denied the charges.
Therefore, trial was conducted.
In support of the case of the prosecution, PWs.1 to 14 were examined, Exs.P1 to 14 were marked.
On their examination under Section 313 of Cr.P.C., accused did not plead any defence evidence.

7. The trial Court on hearing the parties by the impugned judgment and order, acquitted the accused on the ground that the prosecution has failed to prove the charges beyond reasonable doubt and the prosecution evidence is full of material contradictions and inconsistencies.
Submissions of Sri.
Shankar H.S. learned HCGP 8. PW1 the victim of sexual assault has supported the case of the prosecution.
Her evidence was corroborated by the evidence of PWs.2 to 4, 7 and the Doctor PW6.
By such evidence, the prosecution discharged its initial burden of proving the charges.
Under such circumstances Sections 29 and 30 of the POCSO Act confers presumption of the guilt of the accused.
It was for them to rebut such presumption which they failed to do.
The trial Court committed error in disbelieving the evidence of material witnesses without stating what were those material contradictions.
The judgment of the trial Court is contrary to the evidence on record and Sections 29 & 30 of the POCSO Act.
Submission of Smt. Raksha Keerthana K learned counsel for 9.
Under the POCSO Act, the prosecution is required to prove that the victim was aged below 18 years.
The same was not proved by the prosecution.
There was delay in filing the complaint which was not explained.
The evidence on record shows that victim was aged above 18 years.
The evidence on record shows that the marriage of PW1 was already fixed with one Avinash and that was broken.

The evidence on record further shows that PWs.2 to 4 and 7 under the misconception that accused No.1 is responsible for such breaking of the proposed marriage, have falsely implicated accused Nos.1 to 3 in the case.
Against accused Nos.2 and 3, absolutely there was no evidence.
Section 370 of IPC does not apply at all.
The evidence of PW2 itself shows that at the time of incident his elder daughter was under post natal care in the house.
Therefore, the case that the first accused dragged the victim forcibly from the house stood falsified.
This is an appeal against the order of acquittal.
In such case the scope of interference is very minimal.
There are no grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and order of the trial Court.

sentences.text: It is the settled position of law that in the appeal against the order of acquittal, the scope of interference by the appellate Court is very limited.
Unless it is shown that the impugned judgment and order of acquittal suffer perversity leading to miscarriage of justice the same cannot be interfered.
Merely because the other view is probable, the appellate Court cannot interfere with the order of acquittal.
In the light of such legal position, this Court has to examine whether in acquitting the accused the trial Court committed any perversity.

11. The case of the prosecution was based on the following evidence:
 i) PW1 the victim.
 ii) PW2 the complainant and father of PW1.
iii) PWs.3 & 4 the alleged eye witnesses.
iv) PW5 the Doctor who examined accused No.1 and issued report Ex.P7.
v) PW.6 the Doctor who examined PW1 and issued the report Ex.P1 and opinion Ex.P8.
 vi) PW7 the mother of PW1.
 vii) PW8 the panchas to Spot mahazar Ex.P2.
viii) PW9 the head master of Government Higher Primary School, who issued issued school admission certificate of PW1 and accused No.1.
ix) PW10 the panchayat development officer who issued Ex.P12 the katha register extract of the alleged of scene of offence.
x) PW11 the woman police constable who escorted PW1 for medical examination.
xi) PW12 the police constable who escorted accused No.1 for medical examination.
xii) PW13 the IO who conducted the investigation and filed the charge sheet.

xiii) PW14 the PSI who received complaint Ex.P5 and registered FIR Ex.P6.
12.

Since the case involves the offence under section 6 of the POCSO Act, the prosecution is required to establish the following facts:
i) That PW1 the victim at the time of offence was aged below 18 years.

4 ii) Accused No.1 committed criminal tresspass into the house of PWs.1, 2 and 7 iii) That accused No.1 committed penetrative sexual assault on her.
iv) Accused Nos.2 and 3 abetted accused No.1 to commit penetrative sexual assault.
Reg. Age:
13.
As per complaint Ex.P5 at the time of offence PW1 was aged 17 years.

To prove the age of the victim the prosecution relies on evidence of PWs.1, 2 and 7, Ex.P5 the complaint, Ex.P1 and P8, the medical reports, evidence of PW6 and the evidence of PW9 the head master and Ex.P10 the age certificate.

14. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgment of Mahadeo s/o Kerba Makse vs.
State of Maharastra and

sentences.text: another held that the factors relevant to the determination of the age of Juvenile in conflict with law are also applicable to determine the age of the prosecutrix/the victim of sexual assault.

In para 12 of the judgment, while referring to Rule 12 of Juvenile Justice (care and protection of children) Rules, 2007 it was held as follows:
"12.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (care and protection of children) Rules, 2007
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
We can also in this connection make a reference to a statutory provision contained in the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Rules, 2007,
where under Rule 12, the procedure to be followed in determining the age of a juvenile has been set out.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Rules, 2007
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
We can usefully refer to the said provision in this context,
(2013) 14SCC 637 - 10 - inasmuch as under Rule 12 (3) of the said Rules, it is stated that:
"12.(3) In every case concerning a child or juvenile in conflict with law, the age determination inquiry shall be conducted by the Court or the Board or, as the case may be, by the committee by seeking evidence by obtaining- (a)(i) the matriculation or equivalent certificates, if available; and in the absence whereof;
(ii) the date of birth certificate from the school (other than a play school); first attended; and in the absence whereof;
(iii) the birth certificate given by a corporation or a municipal authority or a panchayat:"
State Of Karnataka vs Mahesha on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76233608/
5
Under Rule 12(3)(b), it is specifically provided that only in the absence of alternative methods described under 12(3)(a)(i) to (iii), the medical opinion can be sought for.

In the light of such a statutory rule prevailing for ascertainment of the age of a juvenile, in our considered opinion, the same yardstick can be rightly followed by the Courts for the purpose of ascertaining the age of a victim as well."
(Emphasis supplied)

15. The above paragraph goes to show that to prove the age of the victim or child in conflict with law,
the prosecution has to first produce and rely on the matriculation or equivalent certificate.
If the same is not available, then the birth certificate from the school first attended by the victim has to be produced.
In the absence of both of them, birth certificate issued by the Corporation, Municipal - 11 - authority or Panchayat has to be produced.
Only in the absence of all the above, the prosecution has to resort the Ossification test.
16. In the present case PW1 after her 9th standard was dropped out from the school.
Therefore, the matriculation certificate was not available.
The next document to be produced was date of birth record from the school first attended.
To show that the admission register extract should have been produced.
But PW9 produces only a certificate Ex.P10 which is said to be issued on the basis of the admission register.
Therefore that certificate becomes the secondary evidence.
As per the evidence of PW9 and Ex.P10, the date of birth of PW1 in the school record was 12.02.1997.
She was admitted to the school on 13.06.2002.
PW9 states that he is working in the school as head master since February 2014.
He is not the person who made the entries in the admission register.
He does not state who furnished the date of birth at the time of the admission of PW1.
No reasons were assigned for not collecting the admission register or admission register extract.
. PW1 in her deposition states that her date of birth was on 12.02.1997.
The date of offence is 17.02.2014.
As per the prosecution itself PW6 the Doctor took the history and other details from PW1 and issued Ex.P1.
As per Ex.P1, PW1 revealed before PW6 her date of birth as 11.03.1996 and the person who was accompanying her gave her date of birth as 12.02.1997.
As per Ex.P1, PW2 accompanied PW1 to the hospital.
The doctor PW6 says that PW1 stated before her that she was aged 17 years two months.
There were material contradictions in evidence with regard to the age of the victim.
18. It is material to note that there was three days delay in filing the complaint.
In the complaint Ex.P5 absolutely there was no explanation for delay in filing the complaint.

Only during the course of the evidence, PW2 tried to say that due to his concern for his daughter, he tried for settlement with accused Nos.2 & 3 and therefore, there was delay in filing the complaint.
The said explanation came into picture only after evidence before the Court.

sentences.text: The evidence of PW1 and her parents show that her marriage was fixed with one Avinash and that was broken.

According to the accused, PW2 and his relatives were thinking that accused No.1 is the cause for such breaking of the proposed marriage, therefore, all the accused were falsely implicated in the case.
The prosecution witnesses admitted in their cross-examination that the proposed marriage of PW1 with Avinash was broken.

20. The evidence of PW6 and Ex.P1 show that the victim herself gave statement before PW6 that she was in a relationship with accused No.1 since six months prior to her medical examination and on 17.03.2014, when they were indulging in such physical relationship they were caught by PWs.3 and 4.
Thereafter, the complaint was filed.
It also indicates that the relationship between PW1 and accused No.1 was consensual one.

Probably due to such relationship, the proposed marriage of PW1 was broken and thereafter, PW2 tried to negotiate with accused Nos.2 and 3 and when that was not materialized, they resorted to file police complaint.

. Though PW2 contended that he took up the matter with accused Nos.2 and 3 and village elders/panchayatdars and then he filed the complaint, the said panchayatdars were neither cited as charge sheet witnesses nor examined.
According to the accused, the complaint was filed on deliberating with an advocate.
PW2 in his cross-examination admits that he got drafted the complaint through advocate at KR Pet.
He also admits that while filing the complaint his advocate had accompanied him to the police station.
It was suggested to him that they insisted accused No.1 shall marry PW1.
It is true that he has denied the said suggestion.
But the above facts and circumstances probablize the defense of accused in that regard.
PW9 does not even state that his school was the first school attended by PW1.

Therefore, the evidence adduced by the prosecution to prove that PW1 was aged below 18 years was not in accordance with the guidelines laid down in Supreme Court in Mahadeo's case referred to supra and thus unacceptable.
- 15 - Regarding the commission of offence:

22. According to the prosecution, when PW1 was alone in the house, accused No.1 trespassed into the house of PW2 and dragged her to a near by abandoned house and there he committed penetrative sexual assault on her criminally intimidating her.
Therefore, first thing the prosecution has to prove is that the accused trespassed into the house of PW2 when PW1 was alone in the house.

Though PW1 stated that when she was alone in the house, accused No.1 dragged her from house and took her to the nearby abandoned house and committed penetrative sexual assault on her, her evidence was not consistent with the other evidence on record.
23. It is the defence of the accused that the elder sister of PW1 during that time was in post natal care in PW2's house.

PWs.1 & 2 both admit that during the said period, the elder sister of PW1 was State Of Karnataka vs Mahesha on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76233608/
7 in their house for post natal care.
PW1 says that her mother used to be at home to take care of her elder sister.

Though she says that at the time of the incident her sister had gone to the neighbor's house, such explanation does not find place in the complaint,
- 16 - in the evidence of PWs.2 and 7 or in the statement of PW1 before the Investigating Officer.
24. Further, the evidence on record shows that the house of PW2 was surrounded by other houses.
Under such circumstance, accused No.1 dragging her forcibly from the house could not have gone unnoticed by the neighbours that too in a village.
PW1 says that the accused committed sexual assault on her stripping off her clothes.
But PWs.3 and 4 the alleged eye witnesses say that when they witnessed there were clothes on both accused No.1 and the victim.
The scene of offence where the alleged sexual assault was committed was hard surfaced area.
As per the evidence of PW6 no injuries were found on PW1.
If she resisted the offence and struggled on such hard surfaced area, in the ordinary course, she should have suffered some injuries.
Apart from that her statement before PW6 Doctor shows that she was in consensual relationship with accused No.1 since 6 months.
Therefore, she resisting such act only on that day creates doubt that too in the absence of any injuries on her.
PW1, 3 and 4 say that when accused No.1 committed sexual assault on PW1, her cloths were torn.
But the Investigating Officer has not collected the same nor she has produced them before the police.
It is not the case of PWs.1 to 4 and 7 that they produced such clothes before the Doctor or the Investigating Officer.
The delay in filing the complaint, the medical evidence and the evidence of PWs.1 to 4 and 7 themselves indicate that PW1 was in consensual relationship with accused No.1.
Since she being aged below 18 years was not proved, such relationship does not amount to aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
26. Further, Section 370 of IPC contemplates trafficking of a person for exploitation.
How the case of alleged sexual assault by accused No.1 attracts Section 370 of IPC against accused Nos.2 & 3 was not made clear either by the prosecution or by the Investigating Officer.
Charge sheeting them or charging them for the said offence is wholly misconceived.
When the offence of alleged trespass and sexual assault themselves were not proved by cogent and consistent evidence, the other charges under Sections 506 and 114 of IPC also have no legs to stand.
The trial Court - 18 - though did not discuss all the above facts elaborately, the ultimate conclusion arrived at by the trial Court is correct and that does not call for interference of this Court.

Hence the following:
ORDER
The appeal is dismissed.
